disposition: Pass as descriptive published-system benchmark research with explicit scope. No data-selection or arithmetic error found in the inspected results. Do not treat it as a CPU-only causal experiment or a retained-profit forecast.

independent_recalculation.copies_check: Every accepted row's Base Copies equals # Cores times # Enabled Threads Per Core. Full-core systems were not accidentally compared using low-copy throughput runs.
independent_recalculation.verified: All per-vendor medians and equal-vendor medians exactly match a separate Python calculation from accepted_records.json. Independent selection from the raw CSV produces exactly 119 rows.
independent_recalculation.date_check: Accepted records have publication months no later than October 2026. Therefore the month-only source field does not create a November 5 cutoff ambiguity for accepted rows. Capture date should still be reported.

methodology.selection: Exact named SKU choice was written before bulk scoring and includes both prior/current Intel packages and selected AMD competitors. That controls a limited research question; it is not a representative survey of every shipping CPU or actual sales mix.
methodology.output_units: SPECrate2017_int_base is a dimensionless normalized throughput metric, not GHz, operations per second, per-core IPC, inference tokens or an agentic-workload metric. Never describe a 1.1x ratio as universal application performance.
methodology.baseline: Using Base avoids mixing Peak scores. Base still permits compiler- and architecture-specific implementations under benchmark rules. It is not an unoptimized or identical-binary comparison.
methodology.aggregation: A median of each OEM's submission median reduces repeated-submission weighting, but does not estimate a shipment-weighted population. The same underlying board/configuration may reappear, and OEM overlap does not match memory, compiler, OS, BIOS, power settings or dates.
methodology.system_comparison: SPEC itself states that the benchmark intentionally measures processor, memory hierarchy and compilers together. Those are part of an available system package but confound attributing a result to CPU silicon alone.
methodology.thin_group: 6990E+ has one accepted 2-socket submission; it should be a labeled example, not a stable cross-OEM median estimate. 9996 has no accepted data and must not be assigned an inferred score.
methodology.energy_records: Three accepted records also report energy metrics (6780E Lenovo; 9965 Supermicro twice). Their Baseline field is still the ordinary integer-rate score. Such configurations may reflect different power policies. Do not relabel the energy metric as measured watts or CPU efficiency.
methodology.no_independence: 119 published submissions are vendor-selected configurations, not 119 independent experiments or a statistical sample. No p-value, confidence interval or market-level win probability follows.
methodology.suite_boundary: CPU2017 and CPU2026 cannot be pooled. Absence of a new-model CPU2017 score can reflect the suite transition or submission selection rather than product inferiority.

relevance_to_ASP.supported: The data illustrates that useful performance can rise when Intel package content rises, supporting the plausibility of an upgrade proposition. AMD's higher 9755 median at each shared OEM is a concrete counterexample to assuming broad Intel integer-throughput leadership.
relevance_to_ASP.not_supported: Neither a benchmark score nor recommended list price identifies customer net price, shipment mix, unit elasticity, Intel margin, substrate cost or the share of customer surplus captured by Intel.
relevance_to_ASP.recommended_phrase: Published system benchmarks support a real Intel generation upgrade, while also showing competitive alternatives. The investment case therefore rests on retained economics and delivery, not a claim that Intel wins every workload.
relevance_to_ASP.pricing_caution: Any current recommended-price/score ratio is a dated CPU-price illustration. It excludes the rest of the system and does not measure system TCO or realized Intel ASP.

sources.paraphrase: CPU2017 depends on CPU, memory and compiler. Rate scores aggregate concurrent copies relative to a reference system and combine component results geometrically. Base rules constrain build flags but do not standardize all hardware/software choices.
